relations.statement: The count of syntactic states of the regime, and whether <a> after <> is a new state, is a function of a declared identity convention: opaque gives <> ~ <a> when O is empty (no new state), exact-inscription gives <> != <a> (one more state). Without a declared convention the effect is undecidable.
relations.hypotheses: A declared identity convention (opaque or exact-inscription) chosen by the host; O empty for the opaque branch.

lemmas.statement: For a regime with empty observation set O, the state count under exact-inscription equals the state count under opaque plus one when <a> is supplied after <>; the new-state claim holds iff the exact-inscription convention is declared.
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem two_branch (opaqueCount exactCount : Nat) (h : exactCount = opaqueCount + 1) : exactCount != opaqueCount := by sorry

near_misses.claim: Trials 1 and 2 (opaque) versus the full replay (exact-inscription) are evidence for one convention over the other.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: All three replies are behaviour of one unrecorded model under undeclared conventions; they show relativity to convention, not which convention is correct.

near_misses.claim: With O empty, <> and <a> are not told apart, so <a> is simply not a new state.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: This holds only under the opaque convention; exact-inscription makes the strings differ and adds a state.

open_obligations: Host must declare identity convention (opaque or exact-inscription).
No existing SRC declaration models identity conventions or syntactic state counting; relation and lemma are proposed_new.
Formalize the regime, the O-indistinguishability quotient, and the inscription-level state set in Lean.
Base state count of the regime is not given, so only the +1 difference is claimed.
